unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy, the maximum Vickers hardness of 965.6 ± 7.6 HV was achieved after aging at 600 °C for 6 h (a shorter time than this sample's 10 h); after reaching the peak, extending the aging time to 10 h slightly decreased the hardness to 948.6 ± 12.8 HV (this sample's value). The 600 °C series is the highest among all aging temperatures for the 15Al alloy (Fig. 2).

The α → β-Mn transformation of the 15Al alloy is complete (α matrix almost fully transformed) within about 1 h of aging at 600 °C and above, and in only ~3 h at 525 °C; the resulting ultra-hard β-Mn gives the alloy its ultra-high hardness (253.4 HV solution-treated → up to 965.6 HV).

TEM/SAED/EDS analyses were performed only on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h (the peak-hardness sample, not this 600 °C/10 h sample): it showed near-equiaxed β-Mn, fine FCC Cu-rich particles (rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn, slightly poor in Al) with FCC twins at the β-Mn interfaces, and Cu-poor β-Mn.

Nanoindentation results pertain to the 15Al peak-hardness sample (600 °C/6 h): average nanohardness 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa and intrinsic β-Mn hardness 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa; SEM-EDS of β-Mn in that sample gave Al 14.3, Mn 36.8, Cu 2.8 at.%.

Fracture toughness data pertain to the hardest 15Al sample (peak hardness 965.6 HV, reached at 600 °C/6 h, not this 10 h sample): average indentation crack length 18 μm and KIC = 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 (E = 164 GPa). The KIC of the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels decreases with increasing Al content (8.6, 6.6, 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 for 15Al, 17Al, 19Al).

The specific hardness of the Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu (15Al) alloy reaches 141 HV·cm^3/g at its peak-hardness condition; existing steels and medium/high entropy alloys generally have specific hardness below 120 HV·cm^3/g.
